questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Chance to explore a new culture through various aspects of everyday life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I find that the process from applying for an exchange to actually arriving at the university is extremely poor. There is an absolute lack of information on how to find details about everything from exams to courses and teaching, etc. In general, it seems as though there is very little communication between the host university and the home university regarding teaching practices in Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When I arrived in Milan, I suddenly found that I could apply for many more courses than I had been able to beforehand. The University of Milan had uploaded their new courses under the wrong academic year, so the selection was broader than my initial point of departure. It would have been helpful to know what to pay attention to in terms of how Italians “work” within an academic setting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was challenging to find housing in Milan. The three of us girls lived together, and it was difficult to find something that was both located within the Milan city area and affordable, as rent was expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be quite expensive, and you should make sure to find housing through a legitimate rental portal. It is also worth considering getting a live video viewing of the apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine, we just had to sign a document confirming the arrival date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I’m not entirely sure, as I didn’t really make use of it, but we could always write to Massimo.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The University of Milan does not offer any psychology courses, so I had to take subjects that fall quite far outside my field of study. I was registered for all the courses I applied for, but I wish that the courses for the new academic year had been uploaded before the start of the semester, so I could have applied for different courses than the ones I ended up taking.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you can apply for new courses during your studies, so if you realize that you do not want to take the course you have been approved for, you can always switch to a new one and apply for a new pre-approval.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was easier than at home, but of course you need to get used to the fact that all concepts and terminology are in English.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very different from that in Denmark. It is much more unstructured and laissez-faire. Some lecturers take attendance in class, while others do not. Exam dates change frequently, and students have the option to choose between several dates for when they want to take an exam. There is very little required reading for classes; instead, students have more teaching hours than at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Globalization and Cultural Diversity, Global Social Dynamics, Research Design, Human Resources Management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you find interesting.

questions.answer: Take a trip to Lake Como or Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay overall, but Italians have a very different lifestyle compared to Danes, so I found it particularly challenging in an academic setting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Answered above.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italians are generally very hospitable and helpful if you ask for assistance, and their unhurried approach to life, without constantly rushing, is probably something we could learn from.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Check the course lists regularly, don’t hesitate to ask for help when something is unclear, and be prepared to be flexible, as things may change along the way

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Milan is quite expensive, so be prepared for it to cost a bit :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students and building a great social life. It has been amazing to experience how Italians just enjoy an aperitivo before dinner and take the time to socialize and relax.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic differences.
